hints: Focus on what standard enthalpy change of reaction really means, the heat change for the exact mole amounts shown in the balanced equation.
Look at the equation carefully, it shows 1 mole of $\text{XeF}_6$, 3 moles of $\text{H}_2\text{O}$, 1 mole of $\text{XeO}_3$ and 6 moles of $\text{HF}$.
Check which option describes those exact amounts reacting and forming together, rather than scaling everything down to one mole.
walkthrough:
**Recall the definition**

Great start, let us get the definition clear. Standard enthalpy change of reaction, $\Delta H_r^\ominus$, is the enthalpy change when the reactants react to give products in the mole ratio shown by the balanced equation, all in standard states.

Rule:
$$\Delta H_r^\ominus \text{ refers to the equation exactly as written}$$

**Read the mole ratio**

Now look at what is actually written here. One equation means one set of amounts.

$$\text{XeF}_6 + 3\text{H}_2\text{O} \rightarrow \text{XeO}_3 + 6\text{HF}$$
This means 1 mole of $\text{XeF}_6$ reacts with 3 moles of $\text{H}_2\text{O}$ to make 1 mole of $\text{XeO}_3$ and 6 moles of $\text{HF}$.

**Match to the statement**

So the $\Delta H$ value for this reaction is for all of that happening together. Saying 6 moles of $\text{HF}$ are produced automatically means 1 mole of $\text{XeF}_6$ and 3 moles of $\text{H}_2\text{O}$ have reacted and 1 mole of $\text{XeO}_3$ has formed. That is the full equation amount.

options.A: Incorrect. One mole of products in total would be only a fraction of this reaction. Here the equation produces 1 + 6 = 7 moles of products in total, so this scales the enthalpy change down incorrectly.
options.B: Incorrect. One mole of reactants in total would be only a fraction of this reaction. Here the equation reacts 1 + 3 = 4 moles of reactants in total, so this does not describe the full equation amount.
options.C: Incorrect. This is a common trap. The equation uses 3 moles of water, not 1 mole. The enthalpy change for 1 mole of water reacting would be only one third of the standard enthalpy change of reaction.
options.D: Correct. Well done. Producing 6 moles of $\text{HF}$ means the reaction has happened exactly as written, with 1 mole of $\text{XeF}_6$ and 3 moles of $\text{H}_2\text{O}$ reacting to give 1 mole of $\text{XeO}_3$. This perfectly describes the standard enthalpy change of reaction.
